steps.text: New Year's came and went, but the freezing wind and snow continue to nip at Davistown, leaving not a shred of warmth.
Amidst the crowd outside the plate waiting for their ride, Miles drowsily thinks to himself—how long has it been since he's waited for a bus like this in the cold.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: So what kind of place are you headed to in the frontier, old man?

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: ...Somewhere warmer than here, at least.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Don't worry about me. They showed me mercy by allowing me to be buried along with my old neighbors.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry... I'm so sorry...

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: What's done is done, kid. Best to just move on, and stay out of trouble.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Right, I just remembered. The last time I was waiting for a ride like this, it was to head to a nomadic city to attend my little sister's funeral.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: It was a cold day just like this one. Helena, Woodrow, and Leone... They all stayed with me while I waited for the convoy to show up.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: I was holding a bouquet stuck inside a vase from Helena's diner, and wearing an old suit Leone lent me. Freezed my ass off for hours.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Weirdly, I can even clearly remember how long Woodrow's beard was that day. But everything after I got on the bus is just a blur, like looking through a layer of frosted glass.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: I think I went to a huge city, but it also seemed smaller than Davistown. I think I cried a lot, but it also feels like I didn't cry at all...

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: After that, it's just me hopping on a bus back to town, and my friends helping me get off.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: I actually do remember what happened after that. I went to Helena's place and started drinkin' and drinkin'. Got pretty sloshed, but I somehow still remember everything I said that night.

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: The convoy to the frontier has arrived! Hop on the bus, people of Davistown!
'Even my precious baby sister's gone. All I got left is Davistown, and I'm gonna follow her to the grave, dammit.'
'You hear me, Leone? I'm gonna dig my grave here! And when the time comes...'

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Don't you act like I've forgotten, Miles!

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You told me, 'when the time comes, stuff my body into the plant's furnace, and see if... my ashes can... make the people here sneeze...'
The engineer throws his head back and takes another huge swig.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: As soon as you finished talking, the town was perfectly fine, but I was the one who got the mother of all sneezes.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Haha... Hahaha...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Back then, nobody laughed. Nobody could laugh at all. But now, it seems so damn funny. What do you think?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Don't just sit there all quiet! Drink, Miles, drink!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Sorry we're late.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woodrow, Helena... Where's Leone?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Right before we left, he said he needed some time to figure things out. Said he'd be back later, then popped open another bottle.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...But we're out of time.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: No big deal. If anything... maybe it's better this way.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Tch, damn weather... Why does it have to be so cold?!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Well, once you're on that bus, you can kiss this weather goodbye.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woodrow!

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Ain't nothing wrong with what he said.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: *sigh*... Stop apologizing, Jessica. This whole damn time, it was the bank's fault, Blacksteel's fault, and sometimes, even our own fault. But you... you never did nothing wrong.

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: So stop blaming yourself. We weren't expecting much from you in the first place—
Miles realizes his mistake the moment the words leave his lips, but before he has a chance to explain himself, the convoy leader has already grabbed his arm.

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: If you had something to say, you should've said it earlier! Now get on, you're the last one!

steps.name: Miles
steps.text: Jessica, I...

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: If we wait any longer, I trust you'll take personal responsibility for any Rusthammers or Catastrophes that show up?

steps.name: Convoy Leader
steps.text: Now get a move on!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Don't take it the wrong way, Jessica. That's not how he meant it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I know... But, he's not wrong either...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I've done so much here, but in the end... I never actually accomplished anything.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Nothing changed.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Who is it? Oh, Woodrow? Or is it Helena? Stop rushing me, I already said I'm over it. I'm gonna go see Miles off—

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: What do you want?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Hah, what, you're here to chase me out too?
Unlike what Leone is used to seeing, Sylvia does not apologize, bow her head, and run off.
She stands there for a moment, tightly clutching something to her chest, then stiffly puts one foot forward and walks into the diner.
She keeps walking until she reaches the seat closest to the counter, sits down with her back to the door, and stares straight at the empty chair in front of her.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Mr. Theremin... Are Woodrow and Helena... going to come back?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Woodrow? And Helena? How's that any of your business? They went to see Miles off—
The cold wind blowing in from the crack in the door Sylvia left behind whispers as it circles past the mouth of the empty beer bottle.
It sends a shiver down Leone's spine.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: They went to see Miles off and will be back in a bit. But nobody wants to see you, got it? If you do, then scram. Just... leave me alone.
Sylvia's fingers are tightly clasped together on top of the table.
She gulps down a mouthful of water and forces herself to turn and look at Leone's face. It is then that he finally sees what she had been clutching.
A ring, silver in color, with a few diamonds inlaid across it.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Mr. Theremin, I can't—

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Who gave you that ring hanging around your neck?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The ring?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Couldn't have been me or Benny... So that leaves...

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: ...Him?
Their eyes meet.
Sylvia nods slightly and clutches the ring once again, her eyes burning with an almost crazed determination.
The look in her eyes reminds Leone of someone. Carl's eyes.
The night before he departed, he disappeared for a few hours. And when he returned, his eyes looked exactly like those of the person now in front of him.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: You know, Jessica... our team also has to pull out of Davistown the moment we receive the order. Whatever else happens here, we have to return to the ship.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I know. I know that...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: We're leaving. Miles has already left. Woodrow and Helena said they're leaving too. Leone probably won't stay either... Everyone will be gone.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But I... What have I done for them?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Well, if you ask me... You cleaned up the bandits terrorizing the place, helped Leone save his house, and told Cliff that the bank had overstepped its authority. Even if you don't want to acknowledge it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But in the end... it was all in vain. I... I let everyone down.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Or maybe even worse, it's just as Miles said... Nobody expected anything from me in the first place. It's all because I went and stuck my nose where it didn't belong...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Jessica!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No, even so, I still...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Laura, I need to go out for a walk.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Now's not the time for that. We're about to return to the landship... I'll help you pack your stuff, so just take a nice nap. I'll wake you up when it's time to go, okay?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...I have to do this.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Where are you going?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I don't know.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: You sure about this?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Don't take too long, okay?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I'll try my best.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Stop drinking already, Leone.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: —Wait, you're sober?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: As sober as I ever am.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Wait... and Sylvia? What's she doing here?

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: She insisted on waiting for you two to get back, so she could have a chat with all of us.
Sylvia stands up from her seat, still gripping the ring tightly. Blue veins are visible across her white knuckles.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Helena, Woodrow, Mr. Theremin...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: I know of... some money in the bank.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Of course there's money in the bank. What's the point of telling us that?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: I mean... Blacksteel delivered a large sum of cash to serve as reserve funds. And it's all... sitting in a vault right now.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: The bank wants to prepare for Davistown's new residents.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: They're going to clear out the entire plate to welcome the precision technicians, R&D personnel, and managers that form the cornerstones of the new industries...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: To meet the demand for their deposits and loans, there's... a lot more cash in the bank than usual.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Maybe... enough to let a large group of people start a new life in the frontier.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: ...So, that's the situation.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: That's it? What are you getting at, Sylvia?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...Someone actually sober wouldn't be asking that, Leone.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But here's my question.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If you're saying what I think you are, I need to know.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Sylvia, do you expect us to return the money to its rightful owners?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Or do you want us to take it...?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: By force.
Sylvia nods slightly in an almost unrecognizable manner, then continues fidgeting with the ring on her chest while waiting for the final judgment.
The diner is deathly quiet.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: ...At least we're all on the same page.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Leone, you in or not?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Say something.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: No, I... I know this money should've been ours, but... I don't wanna be criminal scum. Like those bandits.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You really think the bandits were the biggest crooks in Davistown?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So, you're with her, Woodrow?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No?!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I admire her courage, but this is too much of a long shot.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: For example... Sylvia, you got a map of the bank?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Give it here.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: I don't have anything on paper, but I do know that it's a hundred paces from the bank's front entrance to the master control switch. Based on my stride, that'd make it about two hundred feet...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Before that, there are three turns, at steps forty-four, seventy-four, and ninety-three. The landmarks are a potted plant, a floor lamp, and a counter.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: From the master control switch to the entrance of the vault, you have to pass through the reception room, go through a hidden doorway, and then down a thirty-six-step stairwell. Afterward, there will be a straight path, which will take—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You... You actually memorized all that?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Doubtful.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Sylvia, how far is it from your seat to the entrance of the diner?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: I just walked eighteen paces, and after the sixth step, I made a right-angle turn for a total distance of about thirty-six feet.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: She didn't memorize it... She's just been there countless times. As you just heard.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Woodrow, what do you reckon our odds are if you joined us? And what about with Leone?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: How're we supposed to get all this cash out to the frontier without leaving any traces?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I can take care of that.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I don't doubt you can survive out there, but what about the money...?
Helena lets out a sigh. She nimbly hops over the bar counter, picks up the knife on the table, and bends down to pry up the floorboards.
Creak, creak...
Pop.
A cloud of dust, ancient and full of history, rises from her feet.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Don't act like you got me all figured out just 'cause you found that box when the water leaked.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: The man who left me this place as well as his passbook... Any idea when I met him?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Surprise me.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: When I was eighteen.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: At the time, my old man was trying to sell me to his boss's son, so he could climb up the ranks.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: When I heard the news, I ran to the bar and hid there all night, which is where I met him... In the end, we hopped on his burdenbeast in the dead of night and rode until that stifling old place was nothing but a distant memory.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: Wait, you eloped with him when you were eighteen, but by the time you got here...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: We'd broken up. Hadn't seen him for over two decades.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I lived by my lonesome in the frontier for over twenty years.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You think after all that time, I wouldn't have learned how to line my petticoats with goldbacks?
Helena flashes a sweet smile, removes the weapon from her shoulder, and places it on the table in front of Sylvia.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: If you boys ain't in, I'll do it myself.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You and Sylvia... are going to rob a bank? Just the two of you?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Maybe I'll be caught outside the vault, maybe I'll get trapped inside and end up a pile of bones buried in cash. Maybe I'll die trying to escape... Either way, as long as I draw breath, I will see this done.

spans.text: Maybe I'll be caught outside the vault, maybe I'll get trapped inside and end up a pile of bones buried in cash. Maybe I'll die trying to escape... Either way, as long as I draw breath, I

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That's how I'm approaching this, anyhow.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Now, I need to know where you two stand.
Leone takes out a wrench from his toolbelt and places it next to Helena's weapon.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Your move, Woody.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Who's there?!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Jessica? What are you— Why now of all times?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I don't know.

steps.name: Leone
steps.text: You don't know?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But... I need to do something. I need to make a difference.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If what Miles said is still bothering you, you'd best just forget about it.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You still got the time, the energy, to do so many great things. No need to tie yourself down to Davistown and a bunch of old fogeys past their prime.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No, Woodrow...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Too many times now, I've had the drive, but kept falling short for any number of reasons... I didn't have the ability, or the time. The situation changed on me. Orders, or requests.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Even now, I'm not sure what it is I can do.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm stuck watching helplessly as you're all driven away one by one, to an uncertain future in the frontier.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If I don't make a difference this time, I feel like... I might get used to it. To never making a difference.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And if that happens, I can see myself believing—to protect my own mental health—that I've always been incompetent. That I could never protect anyone.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I can see myself thinking there was never any special meaning to picking up a gun. That I'd just made a wrong turn somewhere in life and was stuck with it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I... I don't want that to happen.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: So much so that I'd die to make sure it doesn't.

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sylvia?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: If you truly see this as your last chance... Well, this is also our last chance to take back what's rightfully ours from the bank. Will you help us, Jessica?
As soon as Sylvia stands up, Jessica sees the look on her face.
Her complexion is frighteningly pale, but her cheeks are unusually sanguine in a way that only serves to make the former more shocking.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woodrow? Why are you pointing your gun at me?!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Forget everything you just heard, and scram.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Why? What's the meaning of this?

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: We have to get to the bank...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Sylvia...

steps.name: Sylvia
steps.text: ...and take back what belongs to Davistown.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...Take back?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Go, Jessica. Go back to your friends.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Woodrow!

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You came here for a shoulder to cry on, and we offered you a hot drink and a pat on the shoulder. No more, no less.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You're still young. Every day of your life is a new beginning. I'm serious.
As if her tears had frozen over and evaporated, Jessica's vision suddenly becomes clear.
She sees the unusual blush across Sylvia's cheeks. She sees the wrench and the unfamiliar weapon sitting on the table. She sees the dark hole in the muzzle of Woodrow's gun.
For the first time in her life, she makes up her mind in a split second.
She walks towards Woodrow's pistol, approaches Sylvia, and draws her own gun from her waist before placing it in on the table front of her.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm in.
